h1: Designing Age-Appropriate Zones in Outdoor Playgrounds

props.title: Designing Age-Appropriate Zones in Outdoor Playgrounds
props.summaryText: Why toddlers and ten-year-olds should not share the same structure, what each age group needs, and how to separate zones so the whole play area works for everyone.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: Young child playing in a sandpit

takeaways.text: Toddlers, younger children and older children move and play differently; mixing them causes collisions and boredom.
Each zone needs equipment sized for its users: platform heights, slide lengths and step sizes.
Separate zones with paths, planting or surface colour; a full fence is rarely needed.
Put the toddler zone where carers can sit close by, away from swings and fast equipment.

faq.q: Why should playgrounds have age zones?
faq.a: Children of different ages move at different speeds and need different heights and challenges. Separate zones prevent older children knocking over younger ones, keep toddlers off equipment that is too high, and give older children enough challenge.

faq.q: What are typical playground age zones?
faq.a: Commonly a toddler zone for under-fives, a zone for children of about 5 to 8, and a zone for about 8 to 12, plus areas for teenagers and adults such as climbing nets or outdoor gyms in parks.

faq.q: How do you separate playground zones?
faq.a: With paths, low planting, a change in surface colour or level, or the arrangement of equipment. In busy public spaces a low fence around the toddler area can help.
